item.title: FP's February CE quiz available now to planners
item.description: Keep your general knowledge skills sharp while earning an hour of CE credit toward maintaining industry certification by taking Financial Planning's latest continuing education quiz.

item.title: Older, wealthier clients remain wary of AI. Here's how to build trust
item.description: A new report from Cerulli Associates shows older, affluent investors are far more skeptical of AI use than their younger counterparts. Financial advisors who use AI tools in their practices say transparency is key to setting wary clients at ease.

item.title: Morgan Stanley applies for crypto trust charter subsidiary
item.description: The proposed national trust charter company would be a wholly owned subsidiary of Morgan Stanley. The application was filed on Feb. 18.

item.title: Private markets in 401(k)s face major liquidity challenges: Morningstar
item.description: Private equity in 401(k)s may face significant liquidity strains, reducing returns and complicating plan management, according to new Morningstar research.

item.title: Edward Jones gets green light to launch industrial bank
item.description: The financial advisory firm initially sought an industrial loan charter back in 2020. It's the third company to receive the necessary approvals this year, joining General Motors and Ford.

item.title: DOL moves to undo stricter independence test for brokers
item.description: A Department of Labor rule adopted under the Biden administration had many brokers worried about their ability to work as independent contractors. A new proposal would roll it back.

item.title: If AI is a bubble, how can advisors prepare?
item.description: An increasing number of warning signs point to a potential dot-com-level correction. So, how can advisors adjust client portfolios now?

item.title: Pro-alts dark-money group takes jabs at fiduciary watchdog in report to IRS
item.description: The Pinpoint Policy Institute's public campaign against the Institute for the Fiduciary Standard reflects a mysterious phase of the ongoing debate on private investments in 401(k) plans.

item.title: 5 forces remaking retirement planning: J.P. Morgan
item.description: New data from J.P. Morgan reveals how retirement expectations diverge from reality, and what that means for advisors helping clients navigate life after work.

item.title: Raymond James has 'zero cross-selling' requirements: CEO
item.description: Paul Shoukry said Raymond James differentiates itself by not requiring advisors to push banking and other products and by not aggressively pursuing advisors who leave for industry rivals.
